answers: Google's parent company appears to be satisfied with how Sundar Pichai has performed during his four months as Google CEO, judging by the gargantuan $199 million equity award revealed in a securities filing. Alphabet stated that Pichai was awarded 273,328 Class C Google stock units on Feb. 3, bringing his holdings to around $650 million, reports the Wall Street Journal. The award makes Pichai the highest-paid CEO in America, according to the Guardian, which notes that Pichai's fortune is dwarfed by those of Google founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin, who are worth around $34 billion each, and by that of previous CEO Eric Schmidt, who's sitting on around $3 billion. (A former Google employee was awarded exactly $6,006.13.)

full.prediction:
**Summary of News Passages:**

In 2014, Sundar Pichai, the CEO of Alphabet Inc. (formerly Google), received a significant equity award valued at $199 million, making him one of the highest-paid executives in the United States. The award consisted of 273,328 Class C Google stock units, which were granted on February 3, 2014. At the time of the grant, the value of the award was $199 million, though it has since declined to approximately $182 million due to fluctuations in Alphabet’s stock price.

This new award brings Pichai’s total equity stake in Alphabet to over $650 million. While this is a substantial sum, it still falls short of the net worth of Google’s co-founders, Larry Page and Sergey Brin, who are estimated to be worth $34.6 billion and $33.9 billion respectively, as well as that of former CEO Eric Schmidt, whose holdings are valued at $3 billion.

Pichai’s award is also notable for being one of the largest equity grants by a U.S. company, surpassing the $376 million grant given to Apple CEO Tim Cook in 2011. However, it is significantly less than the $130 million that Google has agreed to pay the UK government in back taxes since 2005, a deal that has drawn criticism for its low effective tax rate compared to the UK’s standard corporate tax rate.

The award is structured to vest in quarterly increments over the next four years, contingent on Pichai’s continued employment with Alphabet. In celebration of the award, Pichai attended the Super Bowl and met with NFL legend Ronnie Lott.

Other high-profile executives at Alphabet also received significant compensation. Ruth Porat, the company’s Chief Financial Officer, was awarded shares worth $38 million, on top of a $30 million signing bonus. Diane Greene, head of Google’s cloud computing business, received shares valued at $42.8 million, adding to the $148 million she was granted in 2013 following the acquisition of Bebop Technologies, the company she founded.
